title: Signal-silence index mismatch causing sparse telemetry gaps across Hosted/Dedicated
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
A set of customer escalations reported missing metrics and intermittent dashboard blanking across Hosted and Dedicated deployments between 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC and 2026-03-10 04:10 UTC. Symptoms included: dashboards showing 0-value timeseries for short windows, live panels with 'no data', and trace spans present without associated metric points, affecting billing and SLO alerting.

Observed behavior:
- Metrics ingestion continued (ingest logs show received batches) but the metrics index selector occasionally returned empty readsets for recent shards, producing gap windows in the materialized timeseries store.
- Issue surfaced for both Hosted and Dedicated customers; Private on-prem customers with older index naming were mostly unaffected.
- Alerts: multiple SLO noise alerts triggered for P99 latency dashboards; one enterprise customer opened a priority escalation with support.

Impact:
- Customer-facing dashboards displayed partial or zeroed metrics for windows up to 15 minutes.
- Alert spam for SLOs and some automated autoscaling actions were affected.

Initial detection and timeline:
- 2026-03-09 22:35 UTC: First Pager alert (metrics-backfill-failure) from our observability pipeline.
- 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC: Support ticket from enterprise customer reporting dashboards blanking.
- 2026-03-10 00:20 UTC: Engineering on-call (Aisha) started investigation; reproduced missing points locally by replaying ingestion from retention window.

Hypothesis and diagnosis steps performed: 
- Compared ingest logs vs materialized store writes: ingestion batches present, but writes to metrics-store DB were successful for older shards and missing for 5 recent shard windows.
- Ran selector query used by the dashboard renderer; observed it returned an empty set when index alias resolution coincided with the compaction/rotation cron.
- Correlated with index-rotation job logs: rotation completed at 22:30 and reused the same index name pattern; a race between rotation and selector read path produced a transient index-mapping gap.
- Found variant index naming logic for Dedicated (includes cluster suffix) that regressed in rollout runtime-1.19.1; selector lookup code path expected canonical alias and failed to match new variant alias during a 1-2 minute window.

Root cause: 
- A race condition between the index-rotation/compaction process and the dashboard index selection code caused the selector to read an alias that had been removed momentarily during rotation. This was triggered by a recent variant alias naming change introduced in runtime-1.19.1 for Dedicated environments. Hosted customers routed through the same code path due to shared routing middleware, exposing them too.

Mitigation performed (hotfix and customer-facing actions):
- 2026-03-10 01:10 UTC: Rolled out a server-side hotfix that adds a 3-second alias-fallback loop in the selector and a guarded fallback to the previous index name. This reduced observed gap windows from ~10-15m to under 30s in canary.
- 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC: Executed reindex-and-backfill for affected 15-minute windows for 7 impacted customers (backfill job IDs logged).
- 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC: Sent customer communications to impacted accounts with incident summary and mitigation steps.

Permanent fix plan: 
- Code change: make alias resolution atomic with rotation by updating rotation job to publish new alias only after the new index is fully warmed and by adding transactional alias swap in the store. Also remove variant alias mismatch by standardizing alias creation across Hosted/Dedicated. (PR planned: github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-store/pull/1842)
- Backfill tooling: add automated integrity scan that detects index alias gaps within 1 minute and schedules a non-blocking backfill.
- Observability: add a dedicated alert 'index-alias-swap-failure' and dashboard showing alias churn, rotation durations, and selector read latencies.

Acceptance criteria for the permanent fix: 
- Alias swaps are atomic and no selector read returns an empty shard set during rotation windows on a 1M request replay test.
- Integration tests covering rotation + selector lookup pass in CI with deterministic timing.
- Rollout to canary env with no downstream dashboard gaps for 48 hours, then staged rollout to production.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Aisha Patel: Continue canary monitoring and complete backfills for remaining accounts (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Marco Rivera: Implement alias-transactional-swap changes and open PR (ETA 2026-03-12 PR draft, 2026-03-18 merge).
- Nia Okafor: Add CI deterministic test for rotation/selector and create the 'index-alias-swap-failure' alert rule (ETA 2026-03-17).
- Support: Draft customer post-incident follow-up and update public status page (ETA 2026-03-12).

Notes and follow-ups: 
- Linked artifacts: Incident notes (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INCIDENTS/2026-03-signal-silence), backfill job logs (s3://redwood-observability/backfills/ENG-275499/), hotfix rollback PR (github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-store/pull/1836).
- Dependencies: rotation job library (repo: metrics-rotation-lib) must be updated in both hosted and dedicated images.
- Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-18 16:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy runtime-1.19.1 with variant alias naming enabled on a small test cluster.
2) Trigger index rotation (simulate compaction) while issuing continuous metric selector reads at ~200 req/s.
3) Observe selector returning empty sets for 1-2 minute windows if rotation alias is swapped non-atomically.
4) Reproduce locally by running rotation job and selector lookup in parallel; use the test harness in metrics-store/test/integration/alias_race_test.go
root_cause: Non-atomic alias swap during index rotation combined with variant alias naming change in runtime-1.19.1 caused selector to miss the new index for brief windows.
mitigation: Hotfix added a fallback loop and previous-index fallback; backfilled affected windows; communication sent to impacted customers.
acceptance_criteria: - No dashboard gaps during rotation in 48h canary run.\n- CI test for alias swap passes reliably.\n- PR merged and deployed to runtime-1.19.2 with standardized alias naming.
